title: Grilled Flank Fajita Bar
seoTitle: Grilled Flank Fajita Bar | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Charred steak, peppers, tortillas, and fresh toppings
subtitle: Charred steak, peppers, tortillas, and fresh toppings
description: Marinated flank steak is grilled, rested, sliced thin, and paired with peppers, onions, and tortillas.

steps.title: Marinate steak
steps.instruction: Rub flank steak with oil, lime, and fajita seasoning, then refrigerate it covered overnight.

steps.title: Preheat grill
steps.instruction: Heat a clean grill to high and oil the grates with a folded paper towel held by tongs.

steps.title: Slice vegetables
steps.instruction: Cut peppers and onions into wide strips so they do not fall through the grates.

steps.title: Grill vegetables
steps.instruction: Cook vegetables in a grill basket, stirring until softened with charred edges.

steps.title: Grill steak
steps.instruction: Grill steak over high heat, turning once, until it reaches your safe target of at least 145°F.

steps.title: Rest steak
steps.instruction: Place steak on a board for 8 minutes so juices redistribute before slicing.

steps.title: Slice correctly
steps.instruction: Find the grain and slice thinly across it; slicing with the grain makes flank steak chewy.

steps.title: Warm tortillas
steps.instruction: Wrap tortillas in foil and warm at 200°F or on an indirect grill zone.

steps.title: Hold safely
steps.instruction: Keep steak and vegetables above 140°F, covering loosely so they do not steam soggy.

steps.title: Open fajita bar
steps.instruction: Serve sliced steak, vegetables, tortillas, lime, and chilled toppings in separate pans.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-cook: turn off direct heat and cover Flank steak — hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven, never below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Log hold time on the pan with a grease pencil. If tones drop after service, cover hot food and keep sides on low heat or ice as appropriate. On return, spot-check proteins at safe internal temp before reopening the line.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers safely
steps.instruction: Cool Flank steak and hot components in shallow hotel pans within two hours — deep pots stay in the danger zone too long. Label with date; reheat proteins to 165°F minimum before second shift. Store cold components separately so textures survive overnight.

proTips: Do not pierce steak while grilling.
Use skirt steak if flank is unavailable.
Label raw and cooked steak trays clearly.
tonightSpread: Set hot components closest to the crew; cold crunch and toppings at the far end of the line.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run.
leftovers: Cool Flank steak in shallow pans within two hours; label with date and reheat to 165°F before second shift.
Store cold sides separately — hot and cold stacked overnight ruins texture.
whyCrewsLikeIt: The grill handles the main cooking while a simple topping bar feeds people at different times.
mealPrepNotes: Make-ahead: marinate steak up to 24 hours and slice vegetables 1 day ahead. Storage: refrigerate for 3 days. Reheating: heat steak to 165°F if reheating leftovers.
substitutions: Use skirt steak for flank steak.
Use corn tortillas for flour tortillas.
